name: input
title: Input
description: Form-associated text and number input with constraints, optional free-text suggestions, token entry, and character counts.

intent.summary: Form-associated text and number input with constraints, optional free-text suggestions, token entry, and character counts.
useWhen: A user must enter or edit one line of text, an email address, telephone number, URL, search query, password, or exact number.
The value must participate in native, Angular, React, or Vue form state.
A compact filter or toolbar needs a single-line search field that follows the shared control-density recipe.
avoidWhen: The user chooses from a finite set of known values.
The user must enter multiple paragraphs or formatted content.
The value is adjusted primarily by dragging within a numeric range.
The value is a calendar date or a clock time.

alternatives.when: The value comes from a finite set of known choices.
alternatives.reason: Select exposes the available values and owns listbox selection behavior.

alternatives.when: The value is a calendar date.
alternatives.reason: InputDate owns calendar date form values, shared Input density, and the Calendar picker.

alternatives.when: The value is a clock time.
alternatives.reason: InputTime owns clock time form values, shared Input density, and the TimePicker.

alternatives.when: The value is an immediate on/off setting.
alternatives.reason: Switch communicates a binary setting instead of free text entry.

alternatives.when: The value is chosen from a bounded numeric range.
alternatives.reason: Slider supports direct range adjustment and communicates the current position.

accessibility: Provide a persistent visible label through the owning field or an external native label; placeholder text is guidance and must not be the field's only label.
Choose the native input type that matches the value so browsers and assistive technology can provide appropriate semantics and keyboards.
Error text is associated with the native input and announced as an alert when the invalid state is rendered.
Read-only fields remain focusable and submittable while preventing edits; inactive or disabled fields leave the tab order and are omitted from form submission.

Password fields keep a named show-or-hide action beside the value. Revealing the value changes only the native input type; the submitted string does not change. The action restores focus to the field after activation.

Optional number stepper actions are named buttons available to keyboard and assistive-technology users. The native spinbutton also retains arrow-key stepping; activating either button returns focus to the field.
Prefix and suffix content must not carry information that is otherwise absent from the field's visible label, value, or description.
A nested prefix or suffix Select is a separate control from the editable value and must have its own accessible name.
states: Every size applies one complete control-density recipe across frame height, inline padding, icon zones, text-container inset, gap, and radius; supporting error content follows the shared 4px field flow.

The normal field boundary uses the shared secondary inset border. Focus promotes it to the thicker bold-brand inset stroke, while error uses the thicker bold-negative inset stroke without changing geometry. Set hasBorder to false only in chrome that supplies enough surrounding structure; supporting error copy then insets to the field's text origin rather than the resting border box. Set hasInteractionFill to false when that containing chrome also owns hover and pressed feedback.

Placeholder text is secondary at rest and quaternary while the editable field is focused because it becomes decorative once typing begins. Single-line placeholder and entered value text truncate with an ellipsis when the field is narrower than its content.
Entered values use the parent surface's primary foreground; prefix icons, prefix text, suffix content, and resting placeholder text use its secondary foreground.
Search fields show a standard borderless CrossCircle icon action only while they contain a value. Clearing emits the empty value and restores focus to the native field.

Password fields show a standard inset Eye action at the field's density. EyeDisabled replaces it while the value is visible. The action stays available on read-only fields and is inactive with the field.

Search fields disable browser autocomplete history, automatic capitalization, autocorrection, and spellchecking by default so browser-owned suggestions do not compete with product-owned results. Consumers can explicitly provide autoComplete when a different native history behavior is required.

Search fields used with owned result sets forward aria-controls and aria-activedescendant to the native field so keyboard focus can remain in the query while assistive technology tracks the active result.

The prefix and suffix slots host compact leading or trailing units such as a currency code, or a nested same-size inset Select. Text adornments use the control's balanced text inset. Nested Selects match the field density, set isInset, hasBorder false, width hug, and indicator up-down, keep a selected value, set allowClear false so the menu has no clear footer, set neutralTrigger so the selected unit stays on the secondary adornment foreground, and do not carry the field's error message. Configurable prefix and suffix controls are separated from the editable value by a vertical divider at the density icon height. The nested inset keeps its 2px remainder toward the line; the editable value keeps the same inline padding from the line as a non-prefixed field keeps from its border. The optional leading icon is decorative and does not replace the field label. Password, search-clear, and date or time actions stay type-owned trailing buttons rather than suffix-slot content.
Use autoComplete, inputMode, and enterKeyHint to provide browser and virtual-keyboard hints without changing the value's semantic type.

Number fields preserve native spinbutton semantics, keyboard stepping, and min/max constraint behavior while dsChange continues to report the native string value. Optional borderless inset Plus and Minus buttons share the field density, appear in that order, disable independently at their numeric bound, and restore focus to the spinbutton after activation. Hide them when direct numeric entry is preferable; browser spinner chrome stays hidden.

textAlign positions the editable value while the numeric stepper stays on the opposite inline edge, keeping the actions clear of the number: start-aligned values use an inline-end stepper and end-aligned values use an inline-start stepper.
The host exposes focused, filled, dirty, touched, invalid, disabled, read-only, and required data attributes for Field integration and diagnostics.
Use Input only on primary or secondary application backgrounds. It intentionally does not expose alternate surface contexts.

Length constraints validate both typed and programmatic values. By default excess text is retained and shown as an error; restrict mode uses a hard input limit. Counters show the draft length and maximum below the field, beside helper or error text when present.
Suggestions assist free text rather than constrain selection. Arrow keys highlight suggestions, Enter accepts one, and Escape dismisses the popup without changing the value.

Tokenized text and search fields use removable double-inset chips and commit trimmed, unique values with Enter or comma, accept delimited paste, and remove the last token with Backspace on an empty draft. Committed tokens submit as repeated entries; value remains the draft and must be committed before submission. Length and pattern constraints apply per token.
responsiveBehavior: Form fields normally fill their parent; use hug width only in a compact toolbar or filter layout with an explicit width constraint.
Choose density from the containing layout: md for ordinary forms, lg for a touch-primary layout, and sm or xs only where surrounding controls use the same compact recipe.
The owner supplies layout constraints and decides when a compact field moves to its own row.

customElements: Listen for dsChange for user edits and dsClear for the search clear action.
Use the form attribute on the host when associating an input rendered outside its owning form.
Bind committed token arrays through tokens and dsTokensChange, separately from the draft value. Assign suggestions as a JavaScript array.
react: Use DsInput, bind value for controlled application state, and handle onDsChange and onDsClear.
Bind committed token arrays through tokens and dsTokensChange, separately from the draft value. Assign suggestions as a JavaScript array.
vue: Use DsInput with v-model for the value, and listen for dsChange and dsClear.
Bind committed token arrays through tokens and dsTokensChange, separately from the draft value. Assign suggestions as a JavaScript array.
angular: Use TextValueAccessor for text inputs and NumericValueAccessor for a statically declared type="number" input. Numeric forms receive numbers or null while the component event remains a string.
For tokenized input bind tokens and dsTokensChange explicitly; value and dsChange represent only the draft. Do not attach a scalar form value accessor to token mode.

styling.rationale: The component owns the protected recipes below; unspecified host properties and application layout remain customizable.

protected.reason: The control density is one atomic recipe; use the size and inset props instead of replacing internal metrics.
The component owns its corner treatment; select the supported radius treatment.
The component owns its surface and interaction treatment; use its semantic presentation props or compose an application-owned surrounding surface.

ariaActiveDescendant.description: Identifies the active descendant while focus remains in the editable field.

ariaControls.description: Identifies the results or popup controlled by the editable field.

hasBorder.description: Show the standard inset border, including focused and invalid strokes.

hasInteractionFill.description: Show the standard hover and pressed fill when the field is not embedded in interactive chrome.

inputId.description: Associates the internal input with an external <label>.

inputMode.description: Preferred virtual keyboard without changing the value semantics.

lengthBehavior.description: Error preserves extra text; restrict uses the browser's hard input limit.

max.description: Maximum accepted value when type is number.

maxLength.description: Maximum text length. A visible counter accompanies this constraint by default.

min.description: Minimum accepted value when type is number.

minLength.description: Minimum non-empty text length, in native UTF-16 code units.

pattern.description: Native whole-value regular expression for text-like input types.

readOnly.description: Keeps the value focusable and submittable while preventing edits.

showStepper.description: Show inset increment/decrement actions for number fields. Native numeric editing remains available when hidden.

step.description: Numeric increment used by native stepping and constraint validation.

suggestions.description: Optional local suggestions; free text always remains valid. Used with text/search fields.

textAlign.description: Align the editable value; number steppers sit on the opposite inline edge.

tokenized.description: Free-text tokens entered with Enter/comma and removable chips. Used with text/search fields.

tokens.description: Committed values; value remains the editable draft when tokenized.

width.description: Width fit — fill the parent (default) or hug the available content.
